items.summary: Mission-ready delivery model: EdgeRunner delivers governed workflows - a bounded pipeline with a standard enforced at each step and human approval at named steps - rather than a model alone. Measured on EdgeRunner's own pipeline corpus, the model accounts for roughly one fifth of the executed work.
items.detail: EdgeRunner's delivery unit is a workflow with a stated guarantee, not a model capability. A workflow is encoded as a WarClaw pipeline (the process), executed by agents (roles with tools and policy), checked by deterministic gates against an approved record, and emitted with a signed receipt. Measured across 17 WarClaw pipelines built from operational requirements: 98 total steps, of which 68 are deterministic code, 19 are model calls, and 9 are conditions - the model is approximately 19% of executed steps. The engineering claim this supports: output predictability is a property of the system architecture, not of model training. Training improves typical output (the mean); bounded architecture is what makes output reliably meet a standard (the variance). A generative step is never deterministic regardless of training. items.summary: RESTRICTED (maturity - do not cite as a capability): WICKET, a deterministic per-claim foreign-disclosure adjudication demonstrator. Decides each statement against its portion markings and a customer-held release matrix, returning RELEASABLE / WITHHELD / UNDETERMINED / HUMAN REVIEW with a signed replayable receipt. items.detail:
RESTRICTED per EdgeRunner direction (2026-07-28): this is a demonstrator, not a capability, and is NOT to be cited in proposals, capability statements or customer-facing collateral. It is deliberately excluded from capabilities.md. Retained in the ledger as an internal record of what was built and measured, so the work is not lost and can be re-assessed if it matures.

WICKET decides, per claim, whether a statement may be disclosed to a named foreign partner. It operates on the fact that releasability is RECORDED, not inferred: portion marking is mandated at paragraph level and below and is assigned by a human with authority before the system sees it, so the boundary decision is a lookup against a recorded attribute rather than a judgement. The decision ladder is default-deny - no citation, unknown entry, unparseable marking, marking excluding the partner, a deny rule, or the absence of a permitting rule all withhold. Derived claims inherit the intersection of their inputs. Absence claims ('no indication of...') route to named human adjudication. Deployment posture is ASSIST MODE: the system releases nothing, prepares the package, and the foreign disclosure officer retains the signature. LIMITS, all material: nothing is certified or accredited, and the package states so; AGGREGATION IS NOT SOLVED and cannot be by a per-claim filter (individually releasable facts may compile into a classified whole) - enumerated compilation triggers only, with residual risk stated on every receipt; the engine is exactly as accurate as the markings it is given; recall is model-dependent (it proves nothing unsafe crossed, not that everything releasable surfaced); the demonstration uses a NOTIONAL policy and corpus containing no real disclosure guidance and no real markings on real material.

items.summary: Assurance by measurement, not assertion: EdgeRunner generates a certification package whose every claim is produced by running a check, including a static proof that no model, network call, clock read, or random source exists anywhere in the decision path. The package is emitted whether or not the checks pass.
items.detail:
For a deterministic decision-gate demonstrator, six checks are executed and their actual results written into the certification artifact: (1) no model in the decision path, proven by parsing the decision-path modules and scanning for forbidden imports, clock reads, randomness, and any import path to the module that calls a model; (2) determinism, by replaying the case set five times and byte-comparing, plus three identical receipt builds compared by signed digest; (3) marking-parser conformance, 27 cases; (4) decision-ladder regression, 24 known-answer cases; (5) a fail-closed property test - 18 malformed, unknown and hostile inputs, none of which may produce a release; (6) proof that a hostile permit-all policy cannot widen release past the markings. An artifact that can only be produced when everything passes is a marketing document, so the generator writes the package with failures in it. Two of the six checks exist because a negative test failed to fail and was investigated rather than accepted. LIMITS: this demonstrates what pursuing certification would require; no authority has certified or accredited the engine, and the policy and corpus exercised are notional.

items.summary: Measured control for information leakage: scoping the model's inputs to only partner-releasable evidence eliminated withholdable content from generated products, tested against its counterfactual - 0 of 5 and 0 of 2 lines withheld when scoped, versus 7 of 12 and 9 of 11 when the same task was run with the model shown everything.
items.detail:
The control is architectural rather than probabilistic: the drafting model is only ever given evidence releasable to the target partner, so leakage through paraphrase or inference is structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely - a model cannot disclose what it never received. Output-side redaction, by contrast, is a probabilistic control that eventually fails. This was tested against its opposite rather than asserted: the identical drafting task was run twice per partner, once scoped and once with the full corpus visible. Live EdgeRunner-26B, stable across repeated runs. Unscoped runs produced claims citing NOFORN material, ORCON material, an unparseable marking and a contradictory marking; scoped runs produced nothing the gate had to withhold. The scoping filter additionally excludes non-approved entries and any category an unconditional policy rule denies, so material the gate would always refuse never reaches the drafter. COST: one drafting run per partner rather than one draft filtered N ways. LIMITS: measured on a notional marked corpus; the figures demonstrate the mechanism, not a customer-environment result.

items.summary: Proven safety floor: a misconfigured or hostile disclosure policy cannot widen release beyond what the portion markings permit. Markings are evaluated before policy and denials before permissions, so customer-authored rules can only ever narrow access - demonstrated against a deliberately permit-everything policy.
items.detail:
This addresses the question an authorising official asks about any rules engine whose rules the vendor cannot review: not 'are your rules correct' but 'what happens when they are wrong'. Because the decision ladder evaluates markings before consulting policy, and denials before permissions, policy is structurally incapable of widening release. The property is proven rather than asserted: the engine is re-run against a hostile policy whose single rule permits everything to everyone, and ten claims whose markings forbid the partner are re-adjudicated under it - none released. This check exists because a negative test appeared to pass for the wrong reason and was investigated. LIMITS: the floor is set by the markings, so it inherits their accuracy; and the guarantee is about the release decision, not about aggregation across separately released claims.

items.summary: Coalition exchange of claims with receipts (demonstrated PoC): the receiving partner independently verifies that nothing it received is marked against it - checking signature, citation integrity and every marking - using only publicly available marking authority, without access to the originator's evidence base or classified release matrix.
items.detail:
Applicable to Mission Partner Environment and combined-command information sharing, where the mechanism has historically been policy rather than a technical control. The originator's full receipt cannot be what crosses a boundary: it names the entries that were withheld and their markings, which can be more sensitive than the product it accompanies. A redacted, separately signed partner view therefore carries the released claims with their entries and markings, the policy identity and hash, and withheld material as COUNTS ONLY - no text, no ids, no markings, and no rule identifiers, since rule identifiers are structure from the classified release matrix. The receiving side, holding no evidence base, no policy and no rules, verifies the signature, that each claim cites the entries listed for it, that every marking parses, and that every marking permits it. That is possible only because marking semantics are unclassified (EO 13526, DoD Manual 5200.01, CAPCO Register). LIMITS: the receiver verifies arithmetic and integrity, NOT the originator's honesty about sources - it cannot confirm the release matrix was applied correctly, that nothing was wrongly withheld, or that a marking is faithful to its source document. Demonstrated on notional data; not certified.

items.summary: Measured basis for keeping models out of verification: a generative model is unreliable as a verification judge. On a hand-labelled entailment set the on-device 26B scored 7 of 10 (its reasoning variant 6 of 10), and 5 of 10 cases changed verdict across identical runs at temperature zero. A governance gate whose answer varies on identical input is not defensible - so verification must be deterministic and the model must sit outside the decision path.
items.detail: This finding is the empirical justification for EdgeRunner's architecture rather than a defect in it, and it is the reason Ground Truth's core is deterministic with no model in the verification loop. Measurement: a hand-labelled (claim, evidence) set drawn from an ICD 203 and unit-SOP corpus, with every label checkable by inspection. EdgeRunner-26B-Nonthinking scored 7/10 with 4/4 recall on contradictions; the Thinking variant scored 6/10 and missed a contradiction. Repeating the identical set three times at temperature zero produced verdict changes on 5 of 10 cases. Both variants failed most often by over-committing to a relationship where the correct label was NEUTRAL. Design consequences adopted: the deterministic citation path is the only route to an attributed verdict; model-judged entailment is recorded as advisory and labelled as such in output; and where a judge is required, a cross-encoder is the preferred implementation over a generative model. The evaluation harness ships with the capability so the measurement can be repeated after any model or prompt change. LIMITS: small hand-labelled set on a single domain corpus - directional evidence about generative judging, not a formal model evaluation.

items.summary: Tamper-evident capability delivery: EdgeRunner ships its workflow library as individually signed, machine-verifiable packages. Each package carries an Ed25519-signed manifest declaring its dependencies, install route, step composition and runtime requirements, and a verifier ships alongside so the recipient can confirm nothing was changed, added or removed rather than taking the vendor's word for it.
items.detail: Addresses configuration management and software supply-chain integrity for delivered AI workflows. Twenty packages - nineteen workflows plus one standalone capability - are published with per-package manifests on a single schema (warclaw-store.v1), alongside a signed registry of forty bundles covering workflows, agent roles, connectors and functions; all forty signatures verify. The manifest is signed over the package's actual contents, so it attests to what shipped rather than to a separate upstream artifact. The supplied verifier recomputes the digest and checks the signature, and treats any file present but not covered by the signature as a FAILURE, not a warning - a package intended to be executed makes an added file the dangerous case, not a changed one. Tamper-tested: modifying a covered file and introducing an uncovered file are both detected and named. Filesystem and sync metadata are excluded by exact filename with the exclusion reported, so verification remains usable on real distribution media. LIMITS: this attests integrity and provenance of the delivered package; it is not an accreditation, and signature validity says nothing about the correctness of the workflow's content.

items.summary: Classification-marking interpretation validated against published authority: EdgeRunner's portion-marking parser handles classification level, SCI control systems and subsets, special-access markings, foreign-government-information markings and dissemination controls, and is tested against a 27-case conformance corpus of which 11 cases are drawn from the CAPCO Register's own published examples.
items.detail:
The marking parser is the component most exposed to challenge, because a silent misinterpretation WIDENS release. Its correctness therefore rests on public authority rather than on vendor assertion: classification levels and control-marking semantics derive from EO 13526 and DoD Manual 5200.01, and the marking grammar from the CAPCO Authorized Classification and Control Markings Register - all unclassified, so the conformance corpus is open and reviewable without any classified reference. The parser implements the Register's category ordering and, critically, the distinction between double-slash category separation and single-slash separation within a category, which naive implementations get wrong and which causes ordinary markings to be rejected. Behaviour is EXACT-OR-FAILED with no partial interpretation: an unrecognised control, an unknown partner or group, or a contradictory marking fails the whole marking and releases to nobody. Special-access markings never widen release. Non-US and JOINT markings are explicitly refused rather than guessed at, because release of foreign-originated material runs on different authority. LIMITS: the Register edition used is v1.2 (2008), which cites EO 12958 as amended, superseded by EO 13526 in 2009 - marking structure is stable across that change, but token lists must be conformed against the current Register edition before operational deployment. Country-specific release determinations are classified and are not implemented in the parser; they are supplied by the customer.

items.summary: First Army operational demonstration of the Ground Truth verification layer on their own mission threads — the basis for the TRL 7 claim
items.detail: First Army ran the verification layer against their own capstone doctrine and their own mission threads, in their environment rather than on a representative surrogate. This is what distinguishes TRL 7 (system prototype demonstration in an OPERATIONAL environment) from TRL 6 (demonstration in a RELEVANT environment) under the DoD Technology Readiness Assessment Guidance. Scope: 1,946 pages across 8 capstone doctrine manuals governed into 3,913 approved rule entries. Result: three documented field failures caught, including a silent 116-to-6 undercount and fabricated doctrine, each turned into a REPORTED error rather than a silent one; 6 of 6 citation-spoof attempts caught with zero false positives; 70 of 70 approved rules anchored verbatim to source; ~2.9s warm at ~3,900 entries. LIMITS: no contract or agreement instrument has been identified for this work, so this is relevant experience and must NEVER be cited as past performance. Ground Truth remains not operationally fielded and holds no ATO of its own. The measured figures are internal-evaluation results, reproducible on request, not certified third-party benchmarks. Confirmed by Bill Bal 2026-08-27; supersedes the TRL-5 figure in the 2026-08-26 adjudication sheet, which did not originate with the CTO. See EV-073 (the capability), EV-094 (measured results and signed WBOM).

items.summary: Proposal Co-Pilot: the Ground Truth ledger process applied to federal proposal development, used by EdgeRunner and four other companies across 30+ federal proposals
items.detail: The same core ledger process that underpins Ground Truth, propose facts into a human-approved evidence ledger then verify each claim in generated output against it deterministically, is in commercial use outside defense, applied to federal proposal writing and validation. Adoption: EdgeRunner plus four other commercial companies, more than 30 federal proposals written and validated to date. The code is distributed as an open-source project, Proposal Co-Pilot, on Bill Bal's PERSONAL PUBLIC repository (github.com/chakmarebel), not an EdgeRunner-owned repository. TWO CONSEQUENCES FOR PROPOSAL USE, BOTH UNRESOLVED AS OF 2026-08-27: (1) OWNERSHIP: do not describe this as an EdgeRunner commercial product or product line; the accurate claim is that the process is in commercial use and has been used to write and validate 30+ federal proposals. (2) DIFFERENTIATION: the mechanism is publicly available, so it does not by itself constitute a proprietary discriminator; what remains EdgeRunner's is the integrated product and the First Army demonstration (EV-130). The four adopter companies are unnamed here and must not be named in customer-facing material without their permission. Cited in the NAVWAR GenAI EPSS solution brief (P10 Technical Maturity, Executive Summary, Company Viability).
